page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply by (coshx − sinhx)/(coshx − sinhx)
steps.why: Multiplying top and bottom by the conjugate (coshx−sinhx) uses the identity cosh²x−sinh²x=1 to collapse the whole denominator down to a plain 1, leaving only the numerator.
common_mistakes: Using cosh²x+sinh²x=1 instead of the correct identity cosh²x−sinh²x=1 — the hyperbolic identity has a minus sign, unlike its circular counterpart.
Forgetting to multiply the numerator by (coshx−sinhx) as well as the denominator.
steps.memory_tip: cosh²x−sinh²x = 1 (minus) is the hyperbolic Pythagorean identity — opposite sign from sin²x+cos²x=1.

steps.label: Simplify and integrate for the final answer
steps.why: ∫coshx dx = sinhx and ∫sinhx dx = coshx are standard hyperbolic derivatives, integrated term by term from coshx−sinhx.
common_mistakes: Writing coshx−sinhx as the final answer instead of integrating it.
steps.memory_tip: ∫coshx=sinhx, ∫sinhx=coshx — the two hyperbolic functions swap names on integration, same as sin and cos do.
